question: Why should your clinic keep a duplicate copy of every referral form you write?

options.A: To replace client health records permanently with blank sheets
options.B: To prove to the government that the clinic is understaffed
options.C: To track which clients have been sent out and who needs follow-up
options.D: To ensure the client pays a fine if they lose the original paper

question: How is the vast majority of oxygen carried around your body in the blood?

options.A: Converted into stable bicarbonate molecules
options.B: Dissolved directly in the blood plasma
options.C: Attached to white blood cell membranes
options.D: Bound to hemoglobin in red blood cells

explanation: You got it! Hemoglobin inside your red cells acts like a fleet of tiny delivery trucks carrying oxygen everywhere it's needed. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h5)

question: A nurse is teaching a patient with high blood pressure how to eat better. What is the best communication style?

options.A: Avoiding dietary advice and focusing only on surgical options
options.B: Handing over a complex medical textbook on cardiovascular pathology
options.C: Speaking in Latin medical terminology to sound professional
options.D: Using simple, clear language and suggesting practical steps like reducing salt

explanation: Keep it simple and practical! Patients learn best when we talk to them like everyday people, not like walking medical dictionaries. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h7)

question: Which type of diaphragm bends easily in half along a central hinge to make putting it in easier?

options.A: Flat spring
options.B: Coil spring
options.C: Rigid ring
options.D: Arcing spring

explanation: An arcing spring diaphragm folds right in half like a taco, which helps guide it smoothly into place over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h2)

question: What physically causes the pulse wave that a nurse feels at an artery?

options.A: Contraction of the left ventricle forcing blood out
options.B: Electrical impulses moving through the heart muscle
options.C: Relaxation of the atria drawing blood into the heart
options.D: Valves closing tightly inside the major blood vessels

explanation: Each time the left ventricle contracts, it pushes a sudden surge of blood into the aorta, creating the pressure wave felt as a pulse. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h1)

question: How are drugs mainly grouped inside the National Formulary?

options.A: By the alphabetical order of brand names
options.B: By pharmacological class and body systems
options.C: By the retail price in local open markets
options.D: By the country where the drug was imported

explanation: Grouping by body systems (like cardiovascular or respiratory) makes it super easy to find what you need during busy ward shifts. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is the immune system called a 'diffuse' system instead of just one single organ?

options.A: It relies entirely on the brain to direct every defensive action
options.B: It only functions when a person is actively sleeping or resting
options.C: It changes its physical structure completely every few days
options.D: It consists of cells, tissues, and organs spread throughout the body

explanation: Unlike the heart which stays in one place, your immune cells are everywhere! They travel through your blood, lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow all at once. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why are grieving individuals more prone to catching frequent colds or infections?

options.A: Grief directly destroys white blood cells
options.B: Infections are a direct psychological symptom of denial
options.C: People who grieve stop drinking water entirely
options.D: Emotional stress suppresses the immune system

explanation: The immense stress of emotional grief lowers the body's immune defenses, making illness more likely. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which of these best describes a nominal scale of measurement?

options.A: Variables contain a true and absolute zero point
options.B: Data points are always ranked from highest to lowest
options.C: Measurements have equal intervals between numbers
options.D: Categories have no numerical value or logical order

explanation: Nominal data is just about naming or sorting into groups (like male/female or blood types). One group isn't higher or lower than another! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T1#GNS217_U4_T1_h2)

question: What are the bumpy swellings on autonomic nerve fibers that release chemicals onto smooth muscle called?

options.A: Dense bodies
options.B: Motor end plates
options.C: Synaptic knobs
options.D: Varicosities

explanation: Instead of neat little single connections, autonomic nerves have string-of-pearls swellings called varicosities that spray neurotransmitters across a wider area. Neat, right? [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h5)

question: What happens to the body when someone goes without sleep for too long?

options.A: Sensory processing becomes sharper
options.B: Muscle mass grows automatically
options.C: Immune function becomes compromised
options.D: Metabolic rate permanently increases

explanation: Missing sleep puts stress on your body and wears down your immune defenses. Remember to get some rest during exam prep week! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h1)

question: Who should be targeted as key stakeholders during this step of mobilisation?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting the local market
options.B: National politicians running for high office
options.C: International pharmaceutical company executives
options.D: Religious leaders, women's heads, and youth representatives

explanation: Local leaders hold immense influence over community behavior and are vital partners for driving health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a thorough initial prenatal booking visit?

options.A: To administer the final dose of the tetanus vaccine
options.B: To perform an emergency delivery for safety
options.C: To establish a complete baseline health and obstetric history
options.D: To finalize the birth certificate before delivery

explanation: Think of the booking visit as your complete roadmap. Gathering all her past and current health details helps you guide her safely through the rest of the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Why should a nurse be concerned if a patient breaks a bone easily from just a minor bump or fall?

options.A: It raises suspicion for underlying bone weakness or metabolic bone disease
options.B: It confirms the patient has normal bone mineral density
options.C: It indicates that the patient has a severe muscular infection
options.D: It proves the patient engages in professional contact sports

explanation: Spot-on! Bones shouldn't break from minor bumps. This is a huge warning sign for conditions like osteoporosis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is it dangerous when communities keep quiet about adolescent sexual health?

options.A: It permanently stops physical growth and puberty changes
options.B: It encourages adolescents to seek out professional clinic advice early
options.C: It forces teenagers to rely on misinformed peers for guidance
options.D: It eliminates all forms of peer pressure in secondary schools

explanation: Spot on. When adults refuse to talk about these topics, teens don't stop wondering—they just ask their friends instead, leading to myths and risky choices. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a routine semen analysis?

options.A: To check sperm count, movement, and shape
options.B: To measure the exact level of circulating testosterone
options.C: To check for malignant cells originating in the testes
options.D: To screen for active bacterial prostate infections

explanation: A semen analysis looks closely at the number, motility (movement), and morphology (shape) of sperm to check male fertility. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h6)

question: What do we mean by 'gender norms'?

options.A: Genetic markers inherited from parents
options.B: Medical guidelines for reproductive health
options.C: Fixed biological limits of the human body
options.D: Societal rules dictating expected behaviors

explanation: Great job! Gender norms are simply the unwritten rules or cultural standards that society uses to guide how men and women 'should' act. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T3#GNS312_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary cause of hereditary conditions?

options.A: Exposure to common bacterial infections
options.B: Changes in the DNA sequence
options.C: Inadequate nutrition during pregnancy
options.D: Poor personal hygiene during childhood

explanation: Hereditary conditions stem directly from genetic mutations or alterations passed down from parents to their offspring. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h1)

question: A clinic nurse wants to increase teenage visits to the reproductive health unit. What is the best step to take first?

options.A: Punish students who refuse to attend the hospital during school hours
options.B: Involve local youth leaders and teenagers in planning the clinic's hours and layout
options.C: Lock the adult waiting room so teenagers have no choice of seats
options.D: Remove all chairs from the clinic to make visits very quick

explanation: Involving the target audience directly ensures the services match their preferences and removes barriers to attendance. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h6)

question: At which stage of the family life cycle do parents adjust to the birth of their first infant?

options.A: Childbearing family stage
options.B: Launching center stage
options.C: Beginning family stage
options.D: Aging family stage

explanation: The childbearing stage starts right when that first baby arrives, bringing brand new joys and sleepless nights! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is integrating family planning into primary healthcare centers important?

options.A: It removes the need for community health education programs.
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to work in large hospitals.
options.C: It ensures that even rural and remote communities can access services.
options.D: It makes contraceptive services exclusively available to the wealthy.

explanation: Primary health centers are right in the communities. Bringing family planning there means even folks in remote villages can easily get the care and advice they need. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h4)

question: A newly diagnosed patient is terrified and refuses to talk about medication schedules. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient immediately to local public health authorities
options.B: Withhold all educational materials until the patient asks for them
options.C: Force the patient to swallow the first dose of pills right away
options.D: Provide empathetic, non-judgmental support and address emotional distress

explanation: Empathy first! Building trust and helping patients work through their fear and stigma is always the essential first step before teaching them about medications. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why are antibiotics NOT recommended for every single case of acute diarrhoea?

options.A: Antibiotics immediately stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.B: Most cases are viral or self-limiting, and routine use causes resistance
options.C: Bacteria are completely immune to all known pharmacological drugs
options.D: Antibiotics always cause immediate perforation of the large bowel

explanation: Most tummy bugs are viral and clear up on their own. Giving antibiotics too often just creates stubborn superbugs and harms good gut bacteria. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which nerve supplies most of the feeling and movement to the pelvic floor?

options.A: Femoral nerve
options.B: Pudendal nerve
options.C: Obturator nerve
options.D: Sciatic nerve

explanation: Brilliant! The pudendal nerve is the main highway for signals traveling to and from the pelvic floor. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h5)

question: What makes amiodarone different from most other antiarrhythmic medications?

options.A: It is completely cleared from the human body within two hours of a dose
options.B: It cannot be given intravenously under any emergency circumstances
options.C: It displays properties from all four Vaughan Williams classes of medications
options.D: It only works when taken alongside a high-fat meal to help absorption

explanation: Amiodarone is a broad-spectrum drug that blocks sodium, potassium, and calcium channels while also acting as a beta-blocker. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse manager rely only on money and bonuses to keep staff happy long-term?

options.A: Pay raises are illegal in most government-owned healthcare facilities
options.B: Extrinsic rewards always decrease the total quality of patient care
options.C: Financial bonuses do not sustain long-term engagement like internal professional drivers do
options.D: Nurses generally dislike receiving extra money for their hard work

explanation: While cash bonuses are nice, they don't replace the deep need for respect, growth, and purpose. True, lasting job satisfaction comes from feeling valued inside. [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is a great community-level nursing action to help manage stress?

options.A: Closing down local markets to reduce neighborhood noise
options.B: Organizing mental health awareness campaigns and support groups
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications to every adult
options.D: Isolating stressed individuals inside regional hospitals

explanation: As community nurses, we shine brightest when we educate the public and create safe spaces where people can share and support one another. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why is being decisive so important during a sudden medical emergency on the ward?

options.A: It stops doctors from entering the patient's room.
options.B: It provides clear direction and reassures the team.
options.C: It guarantees that no equipment will ever break down.
options.D: It ensures the nurse manager avoids doing paperwork.

explanation: When panic threatens to take over during an emergency, clear and calm instructions from a decisive leader bring order and help save lives. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h6)

question: Who holds overall administrative and clinical responsibility for running a hospital ward?

options.A: The senior ward orderly
options.B: The Chief Medical Director
options.C: The hospital head pharmacist
options.D: The Ward Manager or Nursing Officer in Charge

explanation: The Ward Manager handles staff scheduling, clinical standards, and general administrative duties on the unit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is maintaining the cold chain so important in immunization programs?

options.A: To keep vaccines potent and effective until administration
options.B: To prevent the clinic refrigerator from overheating
options.C: To freeze liquid vaccines into solid blocks
options.D: To make the vaccines easier to draw into a syringe

explanation: Brilliant! Vaccines are delicate biological products. If they get too warm, they lose their power to protect children against diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h5)

question: Which tiny glands are found directly on the back surface of the thyroid gland?

options.A: Adrenal glands
options.B: Parathyroid glands
options.C: Pituitary glands
options.D: Pineal glands

explanation: There are four tiny parathyroid glands tucked away on the back of the thyroid, and their main job is keeping your blood calcium levels nicely balanced. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h2)

question: A patient repeatedly misses follow-up appointments because she states she has no money for transport and her partner controls all household funds. What type of abuse is most clearly indicated?

options.A: Physical assault
options.B: Economic and financial abuse
options.C: Professional exploitation
options.D: Institutional neglect

explanation: Controlling funds and restricting access to transportation to keep a partner dependent represents classic economic abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h5)

question: What must legally happen before a nurse can begin last offices?

options.A: Arrival of the mortuary attendants at the ward
options.B: Formal certification of death by a physician
options.C: Payment of all hospital bills by the family
options.D: Completion of the police report for the incident

explanation: A doctor must officially confirm and document death before any last offices or body transfers can take place. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: How might a patient react spiritually after suffering a severe physical impairment?

options.A: They strictly rely on medical textbooks to find inner peace
options.B: They universally abandon all religious thoughts and practices forever
options.C: They may either find deeper comfort in faith or feel abandoned by God
options.D: They automatically experience a complete resolution of existential doubt

explanation: Everyone copes differently. Some lean into their faith for strength, while others might feel angry or let down. Both reactions are very human. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h2)

question: What makes a reservoir host different from a primary host?

options.A: It is always a human being rather than an animal or environmental source
options.B: It kills the pathogen rapidly before any transmission can take place
options.C: It maintains the pathogen in nature long-term, often without showing signs of illness itself
options.D: It requires artificial laboratory conditions to harbor the infectious agent

explanation: Think of a reservoir as a safe long-term hideout. It keeps the germs alive in nature without necessarily getting very sick itself. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which sign is a major red flag for pneumonia or a serious chest infection in an infant?

options.A: Swollen joints and painful movement
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.C: Inability to close the eyelids fully
options.D: Fast breathing or chest indrawing

explanation: Well done! Breathing very fast or having the skin suck in around the ribs are classic warning signs that a baby is struggling to breathe. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h6)

question: A patient is scared they will suffocate when the scope goes into their nose. How should you, as the nurse, respond?

options.A: Inform them that the procedure will be canceled until their anxiety goes away completely.
options.B: Tell them to hold their breath entirely until the doctor pulls the camera back out.
options.C: Assure them that a breathing machine will completely take over their lungs during the procedure.
options.D: Explain that they will still be able to breathe freely through their nose and mouth around the thin scope.

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Reassuring patients that the scope is tiny and their airway is wide open does wonders to calm their nerves. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h5)

question: Roughly how long does the complete cycle of spermatogenesis take in humans?

options.A: About 6 to 9 months
options.B: Exactly 14 days
options.C: About 64 to 74 days
options.D: Exactly 28 days

explanation: The entire transformation from an immature germ cell to a mature spermatozoon takes approximately two to two and a half months. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h1)

question: A young girl who survived breast ironing displays intense social withdrawal and low self-esteem. What is the primary cause of these emotional issues?

options.A: Her inability to understand simple classroom instructions
options.B: Side effects from emergency medications given at the hospital
options.C: Distortion of her natural body image during puberty
options.D: A sudden chemical imbalance in her brain caused by fever

explanation: Unnatural changes and scarring to the chest during developmental years heavily damage self-perception and confidence. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h5)

question: A pregnant client at 32 weeks gestation reports a sudden severe headache and blurred vision. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Suggest she drink more water and take a mild over-the-counter pain reliever
options.B: Notify the primary care provider immediately to evaluate for preeclampsia
options.C: Reassure her that these are normal symptoms of increased blood volume
options.D: Advise her to lie flat on her back for an hour to relieve eye strain

explanation: Severe headaches and visual disturbances are cardinal signs of gestational hypertension or preeclampsia, which require urgent medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: Why are oral medication doses often higher than intravenous doses of the same drug?

options.A: Oral medications dissolve much slower in the bloodstream than IV fluids
options.B: The stomach acid completely destroys most active drug ingredients
options.C: Part of the drug is broken down by the liver before reaching the bloodstream
options.D: The intestines absorb only a tiny fraction of swallowed medicines

explanation: The first-pass effect breaks down a portion of the oral drug in the liver, meaning a higher dose is needed to achieve the same therapeutic effect as an IV dose. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h1)

question: When must a pair of disposable medical gloves be changed?

options.A: Only when they show visible tears
options.B: Before washing your hands
options.C: Between caring for different patients
options.D: At the end of an eight-hour shift

explanation: Gloves must always be changed between patients to prevent carrying micro-organisms from one person to another. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing formal home health care in Nigeria?

options.B: Universal government funding covering all home care services
options.C: Shortage of a unified national health policy for home care
options.D: Public preference for traditional healing methods in some areas

question: Where is the best place to store raw poultry inside a refrigerator to avoid contamination?

options.A: On the lowest shelf
options.B: Directly beside the cooked meals
options.C: On the top shelf
options.D: Inside the vegetable crisper drawer

question: A patient demands antibiotics for a mild viral cold. As a nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Antibiotics will shorten the viral illness if taken in high doses immediately
options.B: Viral infections require broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent secondary fungi
options.C: Antibiotics only target bacteria and will drive resistance without curing viruses
options.D: Antibiotics help the immune system recognize viral proteins much faster

explanation: Spot on! Antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses. Taking them for a cold won't help the patient get better, but it will help breed stubborn germs. Patient education is key here! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h4)

question: What is considered the single most effective approach to managing occupational lung diseases?

options.A: Prescribing expensive daily antibiotic tablets
options.B: Performing routine lung transplant surgery on all workers
options.C: Administering oxygen therapy during night shifts only
options.D: Primary prevention and stopping exposure to dust

explanation: Because lung scarring cannot be reversed, stopping the inhalation of harmful dusts before disease starts is the only foolproof solution. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)

question: Which sign should you teach a mother to report immediately after taking her baby home from a circumcision?

options.A: The baby is unable to pass urine for many hours after the procedure
options.B: The baby cries briefly when the diaper is changed
options.C: A thin yellowish film is visible on the surface of the glans penis
options.D: The Plastibell ring is still attached on the third day at home

explanation: If a baby can't pee, it could mean swelling is blocking the urethra. That's an urgent sign that needs immediate medical review! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h9)

question: Why is obtaining a baseline physical assessment during admission important?

options.A: It gives you a standard to compare future health changes against
options.B: It allows the nurse to discharge the patient much faster
options.C: It guarantees the patient will not develop new complications
options.D: It prevents the patient from asking questions about their care

explanation: Initial baseline data lets the nurse spot subtle improvements or sudden declines during the hospital stay. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is the pre-symptomatic (incubation) stage of a disease so tricky for public health?

options.A: The disease is always fatal during this specific timeframe.
options.B: Infected people can spread the disease without knowing they are sick.
options.C: Laboratory tests are entirely incapable of detecting any pathogens.
options.D: Patients during this stage are completely immune to medical treatment.

explanation: That's right! Because people feel totally fine during this time, they move around freely and can unknowingly pass the germ to others. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h4)

question: What tiny muscle attached to hair follicles pulls hair upright to give us goosebumps?

options.A: Sebaceous muscle
options.B: Matrix fiber
options.C: Arrector pili
options.D: Keratin strand

explanation: You nailed it! The arrector pili is a tiny smooth muscle that contracts when we're cold or scared, pulling our hair follicles straight up. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which hormone surge right in the middle of the cycle directly triggers ovulation?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Luteinizing Hormone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: That classic mid-cycle 'LH surge' is the green light that causes the mature ovarian follicle to burst and release the egg! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the usual recommended length of time to take nitrofurantoin for a simple bladder infection?

options.A: Twenty-one days
options.B: Fourteen days
options.C: A single dose
options.D: Five days

explanation: A short, sweet 5-day course is usually all it takes to clear a simple bladder infection while keeping side effects low. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h4)

question: Which Nigerian government agencies help set and enforce rules for environmental health and medical safety?

options.A: Ministry of Finance and Central Bank
options.B: Ministry of Education and Sports
options.C: Federal Ministry of Environment and NAFDAC
options.D: Ministry of Petroleum Resources

explanation: NAFDAC and the Federal Ministry of Environment work together to make sure healthcare facilities keep our environment safe and free from dangerous wastes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h7)

question: Which type of adverse drug reaction is totally predictable because it depends directly on the dose?

options.A: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.B: Type A reaction
options.C: Type B reaction
options.D: Allergic reaction

explanation: Type A reactions happen because the drug's normal action is just too strong. Because they are dose-related, they are easy to predict! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why are immunization and antenatal clinics such great places to teach mothers about nutrition?

options.A: Doctors perform surgical procedures to improve digestion during these visits
options.B: Patients have extra money to spend on luxury foods when visiting the clinic
options.C: Hospitals provide free meals to every single visitor who walks through the door
options.D: They bring mothers and vulnerable young children into regular contact with nurses

explanation: You got it! Routine clinic visits give us the perfect chance to reach and educate the exact people who need nutritional guidance the most. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h6)

question: How does a dangerously fast heart rate hurt the heart's own blood supply?

options.A: It shortens the resting phase when the heart fills with blood.
options.B: It blocks the electrical signals from the SA node.
options.C: It increases the pressure inside the coronary sinus.
options.D: It causes the aortic valve to close too early.

question: Who benefits the most when a community achieves herd immunity?

options.A: Patients recovering from surgical procedures
options.B: Only individuals with strong innate immunity
options.C: Vulnerable people who cannot receive vaccines
options.D: Only adults who travel to other countries

explanation: Spot on! Herd immunity builds a protective ring around fragile individuals who cannot take vaccines themselves. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h6)

question: What is a key way a nurse advocates for a patient with poorly controlled pain?

options.A: Checking vital signs and ignoring what the patient says
options.B: Telling the patient to endure the pain so they don't get used to drugs
options.C: Waiting until the patient begs for stronger medicine
options.D: Working with the doctor to update an ineffective pain plan

explanation: As a nurse, you are the patient's voice. If their current medication isn't working, speak up and collaborate with the medical team to find a better solution! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h8)

question: A clinic wants to run a reproductive health campaign that teenagers will actually trust. Who should they partner with first?

options.A: International trade unions
options.B: Federal revenue agencies
options.C: Youth-led organizations
options.D: Hospital security guards

explanation: Spot on! Youth groups rock at peer-to-peer connection, making them brilliant at reaching young people who might stay away from formal clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h3)

question: Which hormone is responsible for triggering the milk ejection ('let-down') reflex during breastfeeding?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Relaxin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: You got it! Oxytocin causes tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze, letting the milk flow out for the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h8)

question: What does toxicology primarily study?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies in hospital patients
options.B: The manufacturing process of pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Microscopic organisms that cause infectious diseases
options.D: Poisons and their harmful effects on living things

explanation: Toxicology is specifically dedicated to understanding poisons, how they affect the body, and how to manage those effects. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which medical condition is closely linked to blood vessel smooth muscle staying too constricted over time?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Anemia
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: When the smooth muscle in blood vessel walls stays chronically tight, the vessels narrow and resistance climbs, which we know as high blood pressure (hypertension). Great job working through this set! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the first step a nurse should take when counseling a client on family planning?

options.A: Choose a contraceptive method for the client without asking questions
options.B: Lecture the client on the economic dangers of large families
options.C: Refer the client immediately to a surgeon for sterilization
options.D: Assess the client's medical history and reproductive goals

explanation: Safe and effective counseling must begin with understanding the individual client's health background and personal preferences. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h6)

question: What simple household solution is applied to the cervix during a Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA)?

options.A: Vinegar
options.B: Betadine solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide
options.D: Normal saline

explanation: Yes, acetic acid is just clinical vinegar! It makes abnormal cells turn a temporary white color so nurses can easily spot them. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of control measures in drug administration?

options.A: To reduce the amount of paperwork nurses must complete daily
options.B: To speed up the process of discharging patients from the ward
options.C: To protect patients from potential medication errors and harm
options.D: To help the hospital pharmacy manage its drug inventory better

explanation: Control measures exist primarily as safety barriers to prevent medication mistakes and keep patients safe from harm during treatment. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the main goal of filing an incident report after a medication mistake?

options.A: To collect financial fines from the pharmacy department
options.B: To provide gossip material for the nursing station
options.C: To identify system flaws and prevent future mistakes
options.D: To ensure the responsible nurse gets fired immediately

explanation: Incident reports aren't about blame—they help the team figure out what went wrong in the workflow so we can fix it and protect future patients. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T5#GNS125_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary effect when significant others view healthcare strictly as a response to severe illness rather than prevention?

options.A: The family will spend excess money on elective wellness check-ups.
options.B: The adolescent will develop an obsession with personal fitness.
options.C: The teenager will independently schedule weekly preventative labs.
options.D: The adolescent will likely skip routine screenings and health checks.

explanation: Household health attitudes shape personal habits; if wellness visits are ignored by family, teenagers rarely seek them out alone. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h6)

question: Why is figuring out how a chemical entered the body so important for your nursing care?

options.A: It replaces the need for vital sign monitoring during triage
options.B: It confirms the exact chemical formula without laboratory testing
options.C: It determines the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: It guides immediate decontamination steps and predicts systemic risks

explanation: Knowing the entry route helps you act fast—like washing skin or flushing eyes—and lets you anticipate which body organs are in the greatest danger. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T5#GNS215_U5_T5_h1)

question: A patient has muffled heart sounds and a sudden blood pressure crash after an intracardiac injection. What is happening?

options.A: Normal recovery
options.B: A urinary tract infection
options.C: Cardiac tamponade
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Spot on! Blood pooling inside the sac around the heart dampens the heart sounds and stops the heart from filling with blood, crashing the blood pressure. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h7)

question: Why do we have to be extra careful and double-check our work when giving injections?

options.A: Oral medications require much higher doses than injections.
options.B: Errors can cause rapid and severe harm because absorption is direct.
options.C: Hospital insurance policies mandate double-checking every dose.
options.D: The digestive system neutralizes all injectable substances.

explanation: Spot on! Once a drug is inside the body via injection, you can't take it back out. That's why accuracy is super important. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h1)

question: What is a major focus of care right after a child's heartbeat and breathing return (after ROSC)?

options.A: Discontinuing all cardiac and respiratory monitoring
options.B: Minimizing secondary brain injury and multi-organ damage
options.C: Withholding all fluids to prevent fluid overload
options.D: Allowing the child's body temperature to rise unchecked

explanation: Getting their pulse back is a huge win, but the job isn't done! Now we have to protect their organs—especially the brain—from further stress and damage. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h8)

question: What causes the vast majority of common upper respiratory infections like a simple cold?

options.A: Bacteria
options.B: Fungi
options.C: Parasites
options.D: Viruses

explanation: Common colds are usually caused by viruses (like rhinovirus). That is why taking antibiotics at the very start doesn't help—antibiotics kill bacteria, not viruses! Keep up the great learning. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why might a country with a growing economy still have poor public health funding?

options.A: Private citizens refuse to use public healthcare facilities
options.B: Hospitals are legally barred from receiving federal tax revenue
options.C: Economic growth automatically decreases the total population size
options.D: Government policy priorities may direct funds away from the health sector

explanation: Even if money is being made, leaders can choose to spend it on other things like defense or roads instead of healthcare. Politics matters for nurses too! [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h3)

question: A patient develops a painful, swollen, pus-filled lump at an injection site a few days after treatment. What is this likely a sign of?

options.A: A mild allergic reaction to clean cotton wool
options.B: An expected systemic reaction to vitamin supplements
options.C: A local bacterial infection and abscess formation
options.D: The normal healing process of deep muscle tissue

explanation: Ouch! When unsterile equipment or poor technique introduces bacteria into the tissue, it causes localized inflammation and can form a nasty abscess. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h5)

question: A patient arrives at the emergency ward in severe pain and struggling to breathe. What should the nurse do about medication education right now?

options.A: Postpone detailed teaching until the patient is stable and comfortable
options.B: Force the patient to read a long pamphlet immediately
options.C: Give the medication silently without any explanation ever
options.D: Ask family members to sign a waiver ignoring the teaching

explanation: Severe pain and distress make it impossible to focus or remember things. Always stabilize the patient first before trying to teach! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is the main underlying cause of uncontrolled cell growth in cancer?

options.A: Accumulated mutations in cellular DNA
options.B: Permanent resting state in the cells
options.C: A total lack of cellular respiration
options.D: Eating too many vitamins

explanation: You've got it! Cancer starts when genetic errors build up over time, breaking the normal rules that tell cells when to stop growing. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a major, life-threatening danger of an intracardiac injection?

options.A: Severe chronic kidney failure within two hours
options.B: Cardiac tamponade from bleeding into the pericardial sac
options.C: Total loss of vision in both eyes
options.D: Permanent yellow discoloration of the skin

explanation: Spot on. If blood leaks from the needle hole into the tight sac around the heart, it squeezes the heart so hard it can't beat anymore. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h6)

question: How do simple antacids neutralize extra stomach acid without using cell receptors?

options.A: Through direct chemical neutralization
options.B: By binding to specialized membrane enzymes
options.C: By blocking hormone production in the liver
options.D: Through osmotic drawing of fluid into cells

explanation: Not all drugs need receptors! Antacids simply mix with the stomach acid in a direct chemical reaction to calm things down right away. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is developmental surveillance during routine clinic visits?

options.A: Administering yearly school examinations
options.B: Testing blood sugar levels every morning
options.C: Performing major surgery on newborns
options.D: Ongoing informal observation of child milestones

explanation: Surveillance is the continuous process where nurses and doctors watch for expected developmental milestones during routine contacts. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for placing a patient with severe neutropenia on protective isolation?

options.A: To prevent them from leaving the ward before discharge
options.B: To keep their contagious blood disease away from others
options.C: To shield their fragile body from outside germs
options.D: To reduce the noise level around their hospital bed

explanation: Protective isolation protects a patient who lacks enough white blood cells to fight off everyday germs in the environment. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty during a poisoning emergency?

options.A: Collecting and labeling biological samples for analysis
options.B: Synthesizing new chemical antidotes in the hospital pharmacy
options.C: Ensuring personal protective equipment is worn correctly
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and watching for sudden clinical changes

explanation: Nurses monitor patients, use safety gear, and collect labs, but we leave the chemical manufacturing to the pharmacists! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary psychiatric condition that antipsychotic medications were originally developed to treat?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Schizophrenia
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Schizophrenia is the main condition these drugs were designed for. They help patients manage reality-distorting symptoms so they can function better. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h5)

question: A patient with a complex heart condition requiring open-heart surgery should be sent to which level of care?

options.A: Primary health post
options.B: Maternity home care
options.C: Patent medicine store
options.D: Tertiary health care

explanation: Tertiary facilities like teaching hospitals have the advanced equipment and specialists required for complex surgeries. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: A client using an injectable contraceptive is seven days past her due date. What is the best next step for the clinic?

options.A: Assume she has moved abroad and close her record
options.B: Wait two full years before checking on her status
options.C: Discard her client card immediately to save storage space
options.D: Flag her file as a defaulter and initiate tracking procedures

explanation: Once the grace period passes, flagging the file triggers our tracking steps so we can check in before her contraceptive protection completely lapses. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h3)

question: In which trimester do expectant mothers most commonly feel mixed emotions, or ambivalence, about the pregnancy?

options.A: Second trimester
options.B: Third trimester
options.C: First trimester
options.D: Postpartum period

explanation: Spot on! Feeling a bit mixed up or unsure right when the news sinks in during the first trimester is completely normal. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T004#GNS226_U2_T004_h2)

question: Which group is most at risk for protein-energy malnutrition during the transition to family foods?

options.A: Healthy young adult athletes
options.B: Middle-aged male farmers
options.C: Infants and young children
options.D: Retired elderly office workers

explanation: Young children transitioning from breast milk or formula to family foods are at high risk if their new diet lacks sufficient nutrients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h3)

question: Which of the following is a potential challenge nurses must watch out for when using digital dietary counselling?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever speaking to a doctor again
options.B: It is illegal to discuss food choices over a video call
options.C: It automatically makes all patients instantly lose weight
options.D: Some patients may struggle with technology or lack internet access

explanation: Digital divides are real; older adults or low-income clients may lack the devices or skills needed for video visits. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h7)

question: Why is it important to report medication near-misses and errors through institutional incident reporting systems?

options.A: It helps the healthcare team identify systemic flaws to prevent future harm
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to bill the insurance company for wasted drugs
options.C: It ensures that negligent nurses are immediately fired from the facility
options.D: It provides legal protection for the hospital during malpractice lawsuits

explanation: Reporting errors highlights weak spots in the medication system so safety procedures can be improved. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h8)

question: How does tucking the chin down to the chest help a patient who has trouble swallowing?

options.A: It narrows the airway entrance to protect the lungs
options.B: It relaxes the jaw muscles during heavy chewing
options.C: It opens the lower esophageal sphincter faster
options.D: It increases saliva production in the oral cavity

question: What is the best way to confirm a family caregiver actually knows how to manage a feeding tube?

question: What kind of lubricant should you put on a nasogastric tube before sliding it in?

question: What happens when pyrantel pamoate affects a roundworm's nerves and muscles?

question: When is the risk of getting pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) highest after an IUD insertion?

question: A patient is booked for an elective knee joint replacement. Which theatre is best suited for this?

options.C: Specialized orthopaedic theatre
options.D: General operating theatre

question: Which common health condition is most directly managed by cutting down on salty foods?

options.B: Hypertension

question: What is the main purpose of routine maintenance for instructional materials?

options.D: To increase the market price of the equipment

explanation: Regular care and maintenance prevent damage, keeping your teaching tools clean and ready to help the next set of students learn smoothly! Don't worry, taking care of equipment is just like keeping your nursing instruments sterile and ready. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h7)

question: You are in a busy radiology department with a stable routine patient and an emergency trauma patient who is struggling to breathe. Who gets imaged first?

options.C: Tell the trauma patient to wait in the normal queue
options.D: Cancel both appointments and reschedule for next month

explanation: Emergency and unstable patients always come first so we can catch and treat life-threatening issues right away. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h6)

question: What happens when bacteria become resistant to older, cheaper antibiotics?

options.B: Pharmacies stop stocking antibacterial medications altogether
options.C: Patients require fewer laboratory tests before starting therapy
options.D: Infections disappear faster because bacteria become weaker over time

explanation: When cheap first-line drugs fail, patients face higher costs and sometimes harsher treatments. That's why fighting resistance is so crucial! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h7)

question: Which heart rhythm is considered a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate CPR and defibrillation?

options.D: Ventricular fibrillation

question: Why do scientists make semi-synthetic versions of natural antibiotics like penicillin?

options.C: To improve stability against stomach acid and broaden antibacterial effectiveness
options.D: To completely remove any chemical similarity to the original fungi

explanation: Tweaking natural penicillin in the lab helps it survive stomach acid and fight off a wider range of stubborn bacteria. Brilliant science! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the typical work environment for a public health nurse?

options.A: Schools, homes, and community centers
options.B: Intensive care units and operating theaters
options.C: Private hospital surgical wards
options.D: Hospital emergency triage desks

explanation: Public health nurses practice where people live, work, and study, rather than inside acute care hospital settings. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard nursing check before a vasectomy?

options.C: Screening for permanent reproductive intent
options.D: Evaluating bleeding history and anticoagulant use

question: A patient is scheduled for a hysterosalpingography (HSG). What is the most important preparatory action for the nurse to take?

question: Why is long-term, daily use of sleeping pills generally discouraged for chronic insomnia?

options.A: They stop working entirely after a single night and never help again.

options.D: Patients quickly develop tolerance and physical dependence, and underlying issues remain unaddressed.

explanation: Pills tend to lose their punch over time because the body gets used to them (tolerance), and they only mask symptoms without fixing the root cause of the sleep trouble. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h7)

question: Why do midwives and nurses perform Leopold's maneuvers when a mother is admitted?

options.D: To determine the exact gestational age in weeks

question: A patient asks if fresh eggs and plain milk are okay on a gluten-free diet. What should you tell them?

options.C: Yes, fresh eggs and plain dairy are naturally free of gluten.
options.D: No, all animal products contain traces of wheat protein.

explanation: Pure, unprocessed whole foods like eggs, meat, and plain milk do not contain gluten naturally. Simple and safe! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h3)

question: When taking off your personal protective equipment (PPE) after a procedure, which item should come off first?

options.B: Gloves
options.C: Eyewear
options.D: Gown

explanation: You got it! Gloves are usually the dirtiest item, so taking them off first stops you from spreading germs to your face or clothing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the most accurate way to measure energy use in a critical care patient?

options.A: Indirect calorimetry
options.B: Skinfold caliper tests
options.C: Standard food diaries
options.D: Body mass index charts

explanation: Indirect calorimetry measures the gases a patient breathes out to figure out their exact calorie needs. It's the gold standard in the ICU! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h5)

question: Why do teenage boys and girls need different nutritional care during puberty?

options.C: Girls require virtually no extra protein during puberty.
options.D: Boys have higher vitamin requirements than any other demographic.

question: A patient with uncontrolled pain has a high heart rate and high blood pressure. Which system is causing this?

options.B: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.C: Sympathetic nervous system
options.D: Thyroid hormone failure

question: What is the very first step in the disease surveillance cycle?

options.A: Data generation and collection
options.B: Writing a newspaper advertisement
options.C: Publishing a textbook on epidemiology
options.D: Allocating national budget funds

explanation: It all starts right at the frontline! Nurses and health workers spot and record cases, kicking off the whole surveillance process. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h4)

question: What is the main job of a line diagram when looking at health data?

options.B: To show data that changes continuously over time
options.C: To list the names of staff on duty during a shift
options.D: To compare different categories of unrelated patients

explanation: Spot on! Line diagrams are your go-to tool for connecting data points over days, weeks, or months to track trends easily. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T10#GNS217_U4_T10_h1)

question: A patient tells you they drink alcohol 'only socially.' What is your best next step?

options.B: Document that the patient denies all alcohol consumption
options.C: Assume the patient is hiding a severe addiction disorder
options.D: Ask specifically how many drinks they consume per week

question: For a woman under 35, how long do couples usually try to conceive before healthcare providers look into infertility?

question: What is a unique, tell-tale sign of fat embolism syndrome that sets it apart from other types of shock?

question: How does a patient's desperate desire to recover quickly affect their injection choices?

options.C: It makes them prioritize fast relief over questioning safety practices

question: What directly causes an ischemic stroke?

options.B: A ruptured blood vessel inside the brain

options.D: A blood clot blocking a cerebral artery

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a community health education program?

options.C: To prove that the nurse is smarter than the people in the village
options.D: To determine if the program achieved its goals and identify areas for improvement

explanation: Correct! Evaluation helps you see what worked well and what you can do better next time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why is cutting all fats out of a teenage girl's diet a bad idea?

options.B: It guarantees severe muscle wasting in the arms and legs
options.C: It stops all physical growth and shrinks bones
options.D: It can mess up normal hormone balance and block key vitamin absorption

question: Which of these is a clear example of intrinsic motivation for a nurse?

options.C: Receiving a monthly financial hazard allowance
options.D: Personal pride in providing excellent patient care

question: Which blood vessel carries oxygen-rich blood from the placenta to the baby?
